w: An integrated system of ramparts, towers, gates, bastions, forts and cisterns built across Illyrian, Byzantine, Venetian and Austrian rule to defend the old town. Together with its natural surroundings, it earned UNESCO World Heritage status in 1979, then joined the wider 'Venetian Works of Defence' listing in 2017.
s: Centuries of empires fortified this one walled town
_facts: Combines Illyrian, Byzantine, Venetian and Austrian military architecture
UNESCO World Heritage since 1979 (Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor)
Added to the 'Venetian Works of Defence' UNESCO listing in 2017
The only site of its kind in Montenegro

w: Petar II Petrovic-Njegos, Montenegro's poet-bishop, is entombed atop Jezerski Vrh on Mount Lovcen. He built a church here in 1845 to be buried near Saint Peter of Cetinje; war damage hit it twice, and in 1974 authorities demolished it over Orthodox protest, raising Ivan Mestrovic's mausoleum instead.
s: A poet-prince's tomb, rebuilt over Orthodox protest
_facts: Interrs Petar II Petrovic-Njegos on Jezerski Vrh, Mount Lovcen
Design credited to sculptor Ivan Meštrović
Replaced Njegos's own 1845 church, damaged in both World Wars
1974 demolition of the old church was ordered over local Orthodox objection

n: Church of Our Lady of Remedy
w: Perched on St John Mountain above Kotor's Old Town, reachable only by climbing more than 650 steps. Completed in 1518, it sits over Montenegro's oldest known building, a 6th-century early Christian basilica found beneath it, close to where the old town's main gate once stood.
s: 650 steps up to a church built over Montenegro's oldest ruin
_facts: Completed 1518, on St John Mountain above the Old Town
Reached via a staircase of over 650 steps
A 6th-century early Christian basilica -- Montenegro's oldest known building -- lies beneath it

n: Church of Saint Luke in Kotor
w: Byzantine and Gothic in one small frame, built in 1195 under Stefan Nemanja. Its iconostasis icons were painted in the 17th century by Dimitrije Daskal. Nearby stands the older Kotor Cathedral, raised in 1166 on the foundations of a 9th-century church -- two very different eras of faith standing almost side by side.
s: A 1195 church beside Kotor's older cathedral
_facts: Built 1195 during Stefan Nemanja's reign
Byzantine and Gothic architecture
Iconostasis icons painted by Dimitrije Daskal, 17th century
Near Kotor Cathedral, built 1166 on a 9th-century foundation

w: Austro-Hungarian fort on the Vrmac ridge above the Bay of Kotor, established 1860 and rebuilt into its present form 1894-1897. It took heavy Montenegrin bombardment in WWI, was disarmed before the war ended, then abandoned after Yugoslav use -- now one of the region's best-preserved Austro-Hungarian forts.
s: A shelled Habsburg fort, still standing over the bay
_facts: Present structure built 1894-1897, established 1860
Heavily bombarded by Montenegrins in WWI
Disarmed before war's end, later abandoned
Among the best-preserved Austro-Hungarian forts in the Bay of Kotor

n: Serbian Orthodox church of St Nicolas in Kotor
w: Built 1902-1909 on a site with an older Orthodox church that stood from 1810 until it burned down on Christmas Eve, 1896. The present St Nicholas church rose from those ashes within a decade -- a rebuilding story as much about resilience as religion.
s: Rebuilt after burning down one Christmas Eve
_facts: Predecessor church stood 1810-1896
That earlier church burned down on Christmas Eve 1896

w: Kotor's largest and most important square, its name -- Arms Square -- recalling the Venetian era when munitions were forged and stored here. Today cafes, bakeries, pastry shops and banks ring a space still thick with cultural-historical monuments, the old town's civic heart since the days of the Republic of Venice.
s: Arms Square, where Venice once stored its munitions
_facts: Kotor's main and largest town square
Name means 'Arms Square', from Venetian-era munitions storage
Surrounded by shops, cafes, bakeries and historic monuments

w: Montenegro's only public aquarium, opened June 2021 inside the early-19th-century Radonicic Palace and run by the University of Montenegro's Institute for Marine Biology. More than 8,000 visitors came in its first three months alone, drawn to a research centre built to study and conserve Adriatic marine wildlife.
s: Montenegro's only aquarium, inside a 19th-century palace
_facts: Opened to the public June 2021; founded 2020
Montenegro's first and only public aquarium
Housed in the early 19th-century Radoničić Palace
Run by the University of Montenegro's Institute for Marine Biology

w: Austro-Hungarian fort near Kotor, built 1884-86, its roof carrying a 100-ton Gruson turret, the last of its type. In WWI it duelled Montenegrin batteries on Mount Lovcen, holding out until an Austrian push drove them back in 1916. Yugoslav forces used it as a depot into the early 1990s; open to visit today.
s: The last Gruson turret of its kind, still on its roof
_facts: Built 1884-86, replacing an earlier fort
Roof-mounted 100-ton Gruson rotating turret, last of its type
Fought Montenegrin batteries on Mount Lovcen in WWI
Used as a Yugoslav Army depot into the early 1990s
